To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the through‐plane lattice thermal conductivity of epitaxial ultrathin LCOO films is nearly independent of the OVO orientation and approaches the lower limit for amorphous oxide glasses.
the through‐plane lattice thermal conductivity of ultrathin LSCo is glass‐like and is controlled by oxygen vacancies and Sr substitution.

the through‐plane (i.e., out‐of‐plane) thermal conductivity of epitaxial ultrathin films of La0.5 Sr0.5 CoO3−δ is found to be glass‐like and nearly independent of the oxygen vacancy orientation, and this is attributed to a combination of effects including the presence of oxygen vacancies, size effects, the weak electron/ phonon coupling, and the absence of electronic contribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the fundamental understanding of the thermal transport in epitaxial LSCO, and the findings are expected to be useful for the rational design of high‐performance thermoelectric devices based on LSCO and related oxides.

a novel mechanism to achieve glass‐like ΛLSCO by controlling the OVO orientation and thus the lattice strain, and provides a new approach to design and synthesize materials with low thermal conductivity for thermoelectric and thermal barrier coatings applications.

the fundamental understanding and control of thermal transport properties in epitaxial LSCO thin films, which may provide insights for the design of oxide thermoelectrics and thermal barrier coatings with high efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the glass‐like ΛLSCO of epitaxial LSCO is a result of a combined effect of oxygen vacancies (the most significant factor), Sr substitution (second most important factor), and the weak electron‐phonon coupling within these ultrathin films.
the oxygen vacancies, which induce compressive/tensille strain and thus control the orientation of the OVOs, are the dominant factor that induces a glass‐like ΛLSCO of epitaxial LSCO films.

the oxygen vacancies, which are the main factor controlling the thermal conductivity in LSCO, are not able to induce any anisotropy of the through‐plane ΛLSCO in ultrathin LSCO films on either insulating or conducting substrates, and thus the glass‐like ΛLSCO is a general phenomenon in these ultrathin epitaxial LSCO films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the oxygen vacancies, as a common feature of many perovskite oxides, can induce a glass‐like through‐plane thermal transport behavior, and the thermal transport behavior of epitaxial thin films is not only dependent on the substrate, but also on the oxygen vacancies.

the glass‐like ΛLSCO of the ultrathin epitaxial LSCO is a direct consequence of oxygen vacancies, and the OVO orientation has little effect on the measured thermal conductivity of these ultrathin films on insulating SrTiO3 or LaAlO3 substrates.
the through‐plane ΛLSCO of ultrathin LCO films on insulating oxides is controlled by oxygen vacancies and is nearly independent on the OVO ordering orientation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oxygen vacancy ordering in ultrathin epitaxial LSCO films does not affect ΛLSCO, which has implications for the thermal management of epitaxial oxide heterostructures and devices.

the glass‐like ΛLSCO in LSCO is a result of the combined effect of the oxygen vacancies and Sr substitution, and that the through‐plane electronic contribution to thermal conductivity is negligible for ultrathin films on insulating oxide substrates.
oxygen vacancies, as the dominant factor, can induce glass‐like thermal transport in ultrathin epitaxial films of perovskite oxides.
